a.summary: `Parser.test` marks the deferred `secret` value without skipping it, so any JSON object with `secret` before `encoding` fails to import; this is the bug that makes the mutant unkillable.
a.failure_scenario: `PrivateKeyEncoding.fromJsonPrivateKey(JsonIterator.parse("{\"secret\":\"<base64 private key>\",\"encoding\":\"base64PrivateKey\"}"))` throws `JsonException` instead of returning a `Signer`. `secretMark = ji.mark()` leaves the cursor at the start of the secret value and returns true, so `testObject` resumes reading a field name from inside the value and dies. All five encodings are affected (the committed test iterates all five and asserts the throw). Because the deferred path can therefore never succeed, `createSigner` is never entered with `signer == null && secretMark != 0`, which is exactly why `RemoveConditionalMutator_EQUAL_IF` on `if (secretMark == 0)` (line 137) survives and why the two `ji.reset(...)` `NakedReceiverMutator` rows stay `NO_COVERAGE`.

b.summary: The failure path this commit chose to document instead of fix throws a JsonException whose message contains the caller's private key in cleartext.
b.failure_scenario: An operator writes a ravina/kms signing config as {"secret":"BbMQkQYZspmkytduTWvXEtc4mMURjsekJDvty2WtKeSb","encoding":"base58PrivateKey"}. MemorySignerFactory calls fromJsonPrivateKey(ji), which throws systems.comodal.jsoniter.JsonException with getMessage() = `testObject: expected [,{}n], but found: ", offset: 11, context: {"secret":"»BbMQkQYZspmkytduTWvXEtc4mMURjsekJDvty2WtKeSb","encoding":"ba…` — the complete 32-byte seed. Service startup failures of this kind are logged and shipped to log aggregators, so a two-key ordering mistake exfiltrates the signing key.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
